purpose: Rights- and identity-verified reference/iconographic visuals for navigation and entity orientation. These images are not scientific evidence and do not support historical-origin claims.

policy.display_rule: Reference media may render only when the source explicitly identifies the depicted subject or cult object and reuse rights are source-verified. Every render must show provenance and media class.

items.title: Cult Statue of Zeus Hypsistos, Enthroned
items.description: Roman Imperial-era cult statue identified by the Archaeological Museum of Dion / Wikimedia Commons record as Zeus Hypsistos. Used here only as historical iconographic reference.

items.title: Ancient Egypt stone statue of Osiris
items.description: Photograph of an Egyptian stone statue identified as Osiris in the Louvre collection context. Used as object/reference imagery, not as evidence for any historical-origin hypothesis.

items.title: Odin on his throne with ravens and wolves
items.description: Johannes Gehrts' 1888 illustration of Odin with Huginn, Muninn, Geri and Freki. This is a modern historical interpretation, not an ancient depiction and not evidence for Viking-period iconography.

items.title: Witch riding on a goat
items.description: Albrecht Dürer engraving named on the Commons file as about 1500–1501. National Gallery of Art open-access donation, file NGA 6674. The print depicts a witch. It is not a NOEMA catalog entity and not evidence that the catalog records witchcraft.
items.collection: National Gallery of Art open-access file on Wikimedia Commons (NGA 6674)

items.title: Witches' Sabbath
items.description: Hans Baldung woodcut identified by the Commons file title as a witches' sabbath. Early modern interpretive image. Not a NOEMA catalog entity and not evidence that the catalog records witchcraft.
items.collection: Wikimedia Commons, Web Gallery of Art file WGA01221
